verbalization: The visible evidence suggests that 1,3-Dibenzylurea may interact with Macrophage-expressed gene 1 protein through a series of molecular pathways. The compound is linked to Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1A2, which is a target of (3S,5S,8S,9S,10R,13R,14S,16S)-3,16-dihydroxy-10,13-dimethyl-1,2,3,4,5,7,8,9,11,12,14,15,16,17-tetradecahydrocyclopenta[a]phenanthren-6-one, which in turn targets Macrophage-expressed gene 1 protein. Similarly, 1,3-Dibenzylurea is also associated with Sn1-specific diacylglycerol lipase beta, which is a target of the same compound, and this pathway also leads to the same final target. These findings suggest that 1,3-Dibenzylurea may act through a common intermediate, (3S,5S,8S,9S,10R,13R,14S,16S)-3,16-dihydroxy-10,13-dimethyl-1,2,3,4,5,7,8,9,11,12,14,15,16,17-tetradecahydrocyclopenta[a]phenanthren-6-one, which is involved in the regulation of Macrophage-expressed gene 1 protein. The evidence is consistent across multiple pathways, indicating a potential mechanism involving the modulation of lipid metabolism and anion transport. However, the strength of the evidence is moderate, and further experimental validation is needed to confirm the direct interaction between 1,3-Dibenzylurea and Macrophage-expressed gene 1 protein.
